focus: Wiring, escape hatch and rule-text amendments
answeredQuestions: Per runtime: which hook or plugin event can deterministically detect a turn that ends in a prose option menu with no ask-tool call, and block or re-prompt it? Which events can only observe?

How should this be wired through hook-registry.json, sync-hook-registrations.cjs and the .skilled/hooks/<name>/<runtime>/ layout, reusing the decision-capture adapters, with the loop guard, sync versus async, and the escape hatch?

What exact rule-text amendments should go into communication-handoff.md §4/§5 and AGENTS.md Gate 3 inside the REPO RULES.md ask-surface carve-out, and should the prose fallback stay for runtimes without a tool?
noveltyJustification: Eight findings are new wiring facts and two are a composed amendment set, with the carve-out conflict as the genuinely new constraint.
ruledOut: A blocking guard on every runtime

label: hook-registry.json covers claude, codex, cursor, devin and Pi; DSH registers through .dsh/plugins/repo-guards and OpenCode through .opencode/plugins, so a complete guard needs three registration surfaces.
A new hook is one registry entry with per-runtime bindings; the synchronizer renders the four JSON files and --check reports drift, so generated files are never hand-edited.
Blocking is the absence of async: the renderer emits hook.async only when binding.async is set, and async means background without blocking.
The fallback field encodes per-runtime drift behaviour: Codex Stop rejects unknown hookSpecificOutput keys and takes systemMessage, while Cursor's envelope is permission:allow plus agent_message.
The adapter layout is .skilled/hooks/<concern>/<runtime>/ with Pi and DSH real files behind symlinks in .pi/extensions and .dsh/plugins/repo-guards/adapters.
The loop guard is stop_hook_active plus a per-turn marker; Claude caps consecutive continuations at 8, so the adapter must approve when stop_hook_active is true.
The escape hatch already exists: isHookEnabled('ask-surface') resolves SYSTEM_ASK_SURFACE_DISABLED, the master SYSTEM_HOOKS_DISABLED disables everything, and env wins over hook-flags.env.
Naming a tool in AGENTS.md Gate 3 would breach the ask-surface carve-out, which makes communication-handoff.md §5 the only place a tool name may appear; Gate 3 must reference §5 instead.
communication-handoff.md §5 is stale for OpenCode (name not recorded; it is question) and its fallback sentence sanctions a prose numbered list for any runtime without a surface.

Amendment set: §4 adds ask-through-§5, §5 updates the runtime rows and narrows the fallback to no-surface or unavailable-surface sessions, and Gate 3 references §5 while keeping A/B/C/D as option labels.

direction: A blocking guard on every runtime
reason: Only Claude Code and DSH expose a turn-end seam; the rest get observe-only adapters plus rule text.
It breaches the ask-surface carve-out and duplicates a table §5 already owns.
Claude subagents, DSH headless runs and codex exec have no ask tool, so a rule with no fallback would be unsatisfiable there.
